_policy: Ceilings are guardrails, not reduction targets.
When a file exceeds its type target, its ceiling freezes at the size it had
when the debt was recorded. Raising a frozen ceiling is a reviewable diff and
needs a justification in the commit message. The ladder is: relocate the
content to its proper tier, then condense it, and only then raise the ceiling.
A too-low ceiling is a budget bug, not a win.
Budgets are in bytes. Bytes are deterministic and dependency-free. Word counts
undercount fenced code, which costs more tokens per word than prose does.

frozen._why: Authored before the rule/record split in #22. Each states its own rationale inline; that prose moves to a decision record and these ceilings come down with it.
